summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 62% YoY to about INR142 crores; FY26 revenue up 87% to INR485 crores, but margins fell and management guided to similar growth in FY27.
summary.overview: Management reported its strongest quarter yet, with Q4 revenue of about INR142 crores (up 62% YoY) and profit of about INR9.5 crores. For FY26, revenue rose 87% to INR485 crores, PBT rose from INR10 crores to INR28 crores, and EBITDA rose from INR38 crores to INR66 crores. Margins were lower than previously guided, which management attributed to qualification and investment costs for new semiconductor and space customers. Management guided to similar growth in FY27 and said margins would improve, and it is pursuing a QIP sized at about 7-10% of market cap.

financial_highlights.change: 87% YoY from INR259 crores in FY25

financial_highlights.value: 15.5% of revenue in FY26 (about 15% as stated)

financial_highlights.change: inventory up 45% vs revenue up 87%; down from about 10 months historically

financial_highlights.value: confirmed POs about INR715 crores; strategic agreements about INR3,000 crores
financial_highlights.change: orders received in FY26 about INR570 crores

segments.name: Aerospace and defense
segments.commentary: Management said the split for FY27 is about 50% aerospace and defense and 50% non-aerospace and defense. Confirmed POs are roughly 50:50 between aerospace and defense and non-aerospace/defense. Boeing program: about INR75 crores executed in FY26 with about INR70 crores left for FY27, weighted to the first two quarters.

segments.name: Semiconductor
segments.commentary: Ramped up after customer qualification in Q2 FY26; management expects 300-400% revenue growth in FY27. Semiconductor and space together were about 20% of FY26 revenue. Current work is wire harnesses only. A second, large semiconductor customer is being onboarded.

segments.name: Space
segments.commentary: Landmark multi-year space contract of about INR400 crores won in FY26; first large production batches executed. Management expects 300-400% growth in FY27, with the customer base being expanded, including Amazon as the current customer.

segments.name: MRO
segments.commentary: AS9110 MRO certification and DPL licence obtained; initial Indian defence and aerospace orders are modest. No revenue number was given; management said pickup would come in coming quarters.

guidance_outlook: Management expects FY27 revenue growth similar to FY26's 87%, i.e. roughly 80-90%, but declined to give a specific revenue figure.

Management said margins will improve in FY27 on EBITDA and PBT. It reiterated that margins in current competencies are 17-22%, with MRO higher, and said phase two (electromechanical integrated systems) could reach 21-30%, targeted for 2028-29.
Management said semiconductor could reach US$200 million revenue in 3-5 years.
Management said the long-term target is to increase content share on existing platforms 3-5x, starting around 2028.
Management said commercial aerospace RFPs are expected by Q2 FY27, with larger orders but smaller first-year revenue.
Management said inventory coverage will fall from 7.67 months toward 4 months over time.
capex_capacity: The company is leasing an additional facility of about 210,000 sq ft near existing operations instead of building new, to speed up readiness; space and semiconductor programs will migrate there.
The QIP is targeted at about 7-10% of market cap; use of funds is capacity expansion, operational infrastructure and working capital.
The company is evaluating ways to strengthen Rossell Techsys Inc. (US subsidiary, RTI) to meet space customer demand.
Boeing T-7 program: strategic agreements of about USD 200 million; production ramp expected later in FY27 (Zeena Philip).
demand_pricing: Bids of about INR4,500 crores were submitted across aerospace, defence, space and semiconductor during FY26.
Export share is about 98% of revenue; about 80% is North America, with growth in Southeast Asia, Middle East and Europe.
Pricing: back-to-back supplier escalation clauses; some customers accept equitable price adjustment (EPA) clauses; advance payments are being sought for long-lead single-source items.
Freight is paid by the customer and all shipments are air-freighted.
Boeing agreed to level-load future schedules.

qa_highlights.question: Why have margins been weaker than guided?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited heavy investment in people, infrastructure and training, and qualification work for new semiconductor and space customers (first article inspections), which costs more upfront and yields revenue in later years.

qa_highlights.question: Will the QIP be used to reduce debt, and how will working capital be managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to cut inventory from 7.6 months toward 4 months. The QIP funds would go to growth infrastructure, operational infrastructure and working capital, sized at 7-10% of market cap.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Boeing T-7 contract and when will it ramp up?
qa_highlights.answer: Strategic agreements of about USD 200 million are in place and orders have been received. Zeena Philip said the ramp-up would begin later in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What are the PAT margin and cash flow expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said cash flow should improve in coming years. The MD said PAT margin depends on QIP timing, and PAT is expected to improve in FY27 if current trends continue.

qa_highlights.question: What share of FY26 revenue came from semiconductor and space, and what are the margins?
qa_highlights.answer: About 20% of FY26 revenue came from semiconductor and space; management said their margins are in the 17-22% range.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company compensate for raw material price changes on long-term contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it uses back-to-back supplier contracts and escalation clauses, with some customers accepting EPA clauses and others not.

risks_watch: Margin delivery: FY26 EBITDA margin was about 13.6% (INR66 crores on INR485 crores) against the 17-22% guided range. FY27 margin improvement needs to be confirmed.
Working capital: inventory coverage is 7.67 months, and the balance sheet is being strengthened through a QIP, whose size, timing and investor are not yet set.
Revenue visibility: the INR3,000 crore strategic agreements are over and above the INR715 crore confirmed POs, and POs are placed on a yearly basis.
Customer and program concentration: heavy reliance on Boeing and a few large space and semiconductor customers. Qualification of new customers is ongoing.
Commercial aerospace entry and MRO revenue are at an early stage, with RFPs expected by Q2 FY27 and no MRO revenue quantified.
Management gave no PAT margin guidance, and the cash flow timeline was unspecific.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on long-term growth, with optimism about the order book and new markets. Cautious and vague on specifics: management declined to quantify FY27 revenue, MRO contribution and PAT margin, and deferred several questions to colleagues.
key_quotes: Financial year '26 marks the beginning of a structurally higher growth trajectory.
Our financial performance in the fourth quarter was the strongest quarter in the company's history.
So yes, our margins will get better this year for sure.
The idea is to keep reducing that moving forward and eventually be a 4 month inventory company.

growth.why: Management targets FY27 revenue growth similar to FY26's 87% (roughly 80-90%, no absolute figure), backed by confirmed POs of about INR715 crores, a Boeing program with about INR70 crores left for FY27, and a 210,000 sq ft leased facility, though the leased space timing is not given and no new capacity is quantified.
